english.title: Trader engage in a commercial practice which was aggressive - Unfair Trading Regulations 2008
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a trader, engaged in a commercial practice which was aggressive under regulation 7 of the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008, in that it significantly impaired or was likely to significantly impair the average consumer's freedom of choice or conduct in relation to a product concerned, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PRODUCT..), through the use of harassment, coercion or undue influence, and thereby caused or was likely to cause him to take a transactional decision he would not have taken otherwise

english.notes:
(i) The Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 were repealed by the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 as of 6th April 2025. For offences committed on or after that date see H101734.
(ii) Aggressive commercial practices are practices which, in the context of the particular circumstances, intimidate or exploit consumers, restricting their ability to make free or informed choices. In order for an aggressive practice to be unfair it must cause or be likely to cause the average consumer to take a different decision.
(iii) The regulations prohibit commercial practices which by harassment, coercion (including physical force) or undue influence significantly impair, or are likely to significantly impair, the average consumer's freedom of choice or conduct concerning a product and cause, or are likely to cause, to average consumer to take a transactional decision he would not have taken otherwise.

other.penalty:
Summary: fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see regulation 14 of the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
